messages:
eng-oncall-bot: PAGER -> token/billing anomaly for tenant acme-enterprise (tenant=t-acme-01) on dedicated pool ded-pool-12 (VPC). token_rate spike >3x, rising 429 quota errors. Paging oncall.
Anya: taking initial triage. Noticed alerts at ~01:12 UTC. Pinging infra and accounts.
Anya: @Sam can you take lead? I see billing alerts + rate-limits stacking.
Sam: here, oncall. What dashboards?
Anya: tenant metrics: https://console.redwood.internal/tenants/t-acme-01/metrics and traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace?t=acme-token-spike . Top symptom: token counts per-request are much higher than expected.
Mike: infra check: ded-pool-12 GPU/hosts healthy, low util. This looks like token accounting increase, not model saturation.
Leo: runtime logs pulled. Many requests include escaped unicode sequences and literal backslashes. Example sanitized payload:
```
{"input": "\\u00e9 Bonjour"}
```
We see the string arriving with literal backslash-u. Tokenizer counts each character, so "\\u00e9" becomes 6 chars instead of 1.
Olivia: cc support/accounting 10. Acme support says they pushed a frontend SDK update (2.5.0) earlier that changed serialization behavior.
Sam: hypothesis: frontend double-escaping or sending JSON-escaped unicode, leading to inflated tokenization. Any quick log grep?
Leo: grep of raw ingress:
```
2026-03-15T01:12:03Z | t-acme-01 | payload="\\u00e9" -> bytes: '\\\\' 'u' '0' '0' 'e' '9'
```
Also found calls with JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(text)).
Mike: confirms billing counters are incrementing; tenant is breaching burst limits and getting 429s. We need short-term mitigation to protect the pool and the customer.
ops-bot: Applied per-tenant burst cap override to prevent global spillover; t-acme-01 capped to 1.5x baseline. See runbook mitigate-token-spike.
Anya: plan of action (short):
- Apply non-destructive input normalizer on ingress to unescape common \uXXXX sequences for this tenant (best-effort).
- Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching where safe.
- Apply temporary billing credit / usage smoothing so Acme doesn't get billed for inflated tokens.
(medium/long): SDK compatibility checks, server-side detection alerts, and postmortem.
Sam: Leo, can you implement a canary middleware to unescape up to 2 levels for patterns like /\\u[0-9a-fA-F]{4}/ ? Must be toggleable and log originals.
Leo: will do. Rolling lightweight middleware onto ded-ingress-1 as a 10% canary for tenant t-acme-01. Command:
```
kubectl -n ingress apply -f ingress-unescape-canary.yaml
# config: tenant_filter=t-acme-01, percent=10, unescape=true
```
Leo: middleware will only perform a safe JSON-unescape when pattern detected; it won't alter payloads that don't match. We'll retain original payloads for audit.
ops-bot: Canary metrics: after 12m, matched requests token_count down ~65% on canary. No apparent errors.
Sam: good. Ramp to 50% and route some debug sessions from Acme to canary for verification.
Olivia: Acme confirms the SDK change: they accidentally enabled an "escape-for-logging" path. They can roll back or ship a patch. They prefer us to keep the middleware while they patch.
Anya: decide: keep middleware as bandaid, but require customer rollback. Also prepare billing adjustment.
Sam: agreed. Ops, apply middleware 100% for t-acme-01 only. Ensure we document changes and have an automatic rollback plan.
ops-bot: Middleware enabled at 100% for t-acme-01 on ded-pool-12. Monitoring token and content diffs.
Leo: most requests now back to baseline token counts. A small fraction still tricky (multipart JSON, encoded attachments).
Sam: updating incident summary: root cause: frontend SDK 2.5.0 introduced escaped/unicode serialization -> token inflation 2-4x. Impact: single enterprise customer on dedicated pool experienced billing spike and rate-limits. Mitigations applied: ingress unescape middleware, per-tenant burst cap, temporary billing smoothing.
Olivia: created billing ticket and proposed one-time credit for window 01:12-01:58 UTC. Waiting acct approval.
Anya: handing off — i'm offshift. Sam, you own the follow-up, postmortem, and customer comms.
Sam: taking handoff. Action items:
- (Leo) Add explicit rollback toggle and telemetry for the middleware.
- (Mike) Ensure cached artifacts didn't persist escaped content downstream.
- (Olivia) Finalize credit and customer-facing incident note.
- (Anya) Attach traces/log links to postmortem.
Sam: I'll file the formal postmortem (INC-2026-00312) and coordinate with Acme for SDK fix validation and rollout.
deploy-bot: Recorded deploy/unescape-middleware v1.0 -> ingress cluster.
ops-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-00312, assigned to Sam.
Sam: closing live coordination. Will re-open if anomalies reappear or customer reports issues. :white_check_mark:
